top5.title: OpenAI losses soar despite sharp revenue growth
top5.description: OpenAI generated 10 billion dollars in revenue in the third quarter, but its operating loss reached 10.9 billion dollars. Revenue rose 50% from the previous quarter and tripled year over year.
top5.why: OpenAI’s $10.9 billion quarterly operating loss despite $10 billion in revenue highlights the enormous funding requirements and financial risks underpinning the generative-AI market.

top5.title: TSMC invests up to one billion dollars in Anthropic and OpenAI
top5.description: TSMC plans to acquire stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI worth up to one billion dollars.
top5.why: TSMC’s planned investments of up to $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI would deepen the strategic ties between leading AI labs and the semiconductor supply chain.

top5.title: Google unveils two new eighth-generation TPU chips
top5.description: Google has introduced two new eighth-generation TPU chips, increasing pressure on Nvidia as competition for dedicated AI hardware intensifies.
top5.why: Google’s new eighth-generation TPUs intensify competition with Nvidia and signal that hyperscalers are accelerating development of proprietary AI infrastructure.

top5.title: Claude Takes on Microsoft Office with New Workplace Tools
top5.description: Anthropic is launching new Claude tools for office work, including Meetings, Whiteboards, Sheets and Data. Claude Meetings can join video conferences and perform tasks such as creating a timeline or looking up figures.
top5.why: Anthropic’s Claude workplace tools target core Microsoft Office workflows, raising the stakes in enterprise productivity and AI-agent adoption.

top5.title: United Bars Third-Party AI Agents from Booking Flights
top5.description: United has restricted access to its app, website, agencies and comparison sites for unauthorized third-party AI agents. The airline cites exposed credentials, accidental purchases and booking errors, among other concerns.
top5.why: United’s decision to block unauthorized AI agents from booking flights shows that security, liability and transaction-control concerns could materially constrain agent deployment.
